Most companies have a CRM.

Most people quietly ignore it.

I used to think that was a discipline problem.

Turns out it's a tool problem.

Here's what actually happens:
→ A lead comes in
→ Rep has to log the call (15 mins)
→ Update the deal stage (10 mins)
→ Add notes nobody will read
→ By the time admin is done, the lead has gone cold

The CRM got filled. The deal died.

Traditional CRMs were designed for managers who want dashboards and reports.

Not for the person actually making the calls.

So reps do the bare minimum — or ignore it completely.

And the pipeline becomes a graveyard of leads nobody's following up.

I came across noCRM — and honestly, the concept makes sense.

Instead of forms and fields, every lead gets ONE thing: a next action.

Call on Thursday. Send the doc. Follow up next week.

No overdue leads silently rotting in the background.
No "I forgot to follow up" moments.

Just a clear list of what to do next.

If you've ever opened a CRM and immediately felt exhausted — it's not you.

It's the tool.
